%1$s has no server and no account with its maker. Nothing about you or how you use the app is sent to its maker: no analytics, no crash reports, no telemetry.

Your chats, channels, files, skills, memory, automations, databases, usage log and settings are kept in the app’s private storage. Keys and tokens are encrypted with the phone’s keystore; they are never shown, logged or put in a backup. Android’s cloud backup is turned off for %1$s.
What leaves it, and where to

The AI provider you chose (OpenRouter, or your own server) receives what each turn needs: your message, attached files, the agent’s instructions and memory, the chat so far and what its tools found. The provider’s own privacy policy applies. On OpenRouter, “Private providers only” (on unless you turn it off) sends requests only to providers that keep no data.
Web search runs through OpenRouter. When the agent reads a web page or uses the browser, that site sees a visit from this phone.
A tool server you add receives the calls the agent makes to it, with the token you gave it.
Dictation uses your phone’s speech recogniser, which may send your voice to its own service.
A backup is a zip you make yourself, saved in Downloads/Apel. It holds everything above except keys and tokens, and it isn’t encrypted: keep it somewhere safe.

The internet and its state (to wait for a connection); notifications (replies, approvals, automations, the budget); exact alarms, starting after a restart, keeping the phone awake and running in the background while %1$s works (automations on time), and all the time if you turn on Keep running in the background; an exemption from battery optimisation, only if you allow it when asked; vibration, for haptic feedback; the microphone, only while you dictate.
%1$s is open source: you can read what it does. Ask or report a problem at github.com/erkanw/apel-agent.
These are shared by all your agents. An agent can switch skills and tools off for itself on its page under Agents, and each automation runs as one agent.

An agent is a version of %1$s set up for one kind of work, like a study companion, a researcher or a training coach. Each has its own name, look, instructions, model and memory. Choose one on Home before you start; a chat keeps the agent it started with.
Your agents’ own folder on this phone. They read and write notes and documents here, and you can open, add, share or delete files yourself.
Written instructions an agent follows for a task it does often, such as a weekly review or a summary in your style. Switch one off when you don’t need it, or ask %1$s to write a new one.
A prompt that runs on a schedule, such as a morning brief or a weekly plan. Each runs as one of your agents and posts its answer in a chat or a channel.

Tables your agents keep for you, such as a reading list, workouts or expenses. You don’t have to build them yourself: describe in a chat what you want to keep track of, as a clear and detailed plan, and %1$s usually sets up and fills the database for you.

What your agents can do beyond writing: search the web, read pages, use a browser, work with your files and databases, and send you notifications. Turn off any tool you don’t want used; some ask you before they act.
A request like one you allowed once runs without asking; only new kinds of requests still ask. Automations, skills and memory notes always ask.
These run without asking only while Approve what you’ve allowed before is on.
Nothing yet. Choose Allow and don’t ask again on a request to keep it here.
Whether each agent may use these is set on its own page.
Chats on one subject kept together, like work, travel or a course. Make one with the + beside Channels; each channel has its own colour and can have its own agent.
